perplexity.description:
Now That's What I Call An Era: (Feels Like) Heaven 1978 >> 1985 (Essential Synth-Pop) is a expansive quadruple-CD (or triple-vinyl) compilation album from Sony Music and EMI, capturing the explosive rise of synth-pop and new wave from 1978 to 1985 across 80 tracks on CD or 43 on vinyl. Spanning electronic, rock, and funk/soul genres, it spotlights a transformative era when synthesizers redefined pop music, blending icy electronic pulses with emotive vocals and danceable grooves. Released in various formats including digipack, deluxe 28-page hardback book, and colorful tri-color vinyl, the set opens with Queen's stadium synth-rocker "Radio Ga Ga," Eurythmics' haunting "Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This)," and Gary Numan's pioneering "Are 'Friends' Electric?," setting a tone of futuristic innovation.

The collection traces synth-pop's evolution through four thematic CDs, featuring icons like Ultravox ("Vienna"), Visage ("Fade to Grey"), Duran Duran ("Planet Earth"), Spandau Ballet ("To Cut a Long Story Short"), and Heaven 17 ("Temptation") on early discs, building to high-energy 1980s peaks with New Order's "Blue Monday," Bronski Beat's "Smalltown Boy," Frankie Goes to Hollywood's "Relax," Dead or Alive's "You Spin Me Round (Like a Record)," and Donna Summer's "Our Love." This curation highlights the genre's cultural shift from post-punk experimentation to chart-dominating anthems, emphasizing sleek production, memorable hooks, and social commentary amid the neon-lit excesses of the era.

Celebrated for its comprehensive scope, the compilation revives the euphoric "feels like heaven" essence of 1980s club culture and radio dominance, earning praise as an essential retrospective for fans of the Second British Invasion and early MTV sound. Its significance lies in democratizing access to remastered hits from a pivotal period, bridging punk's raw energy with electronic dance's polished futurism, and underscoring synth-pop's enduring influence on modern genres like EDM and indie electronica.

title: Now That's What I Call An Era: (Feels Like) Heaven 1978 >> 1985 (Essential Synth-Pop)
